batch: Phase I -- common-noun family-expansion scan for T10 (Places), fully individually reviewed. 296 raw family-expansion candidates (etymologically/lexically related to an existing T10 member) checked one by one against their OWN gloss text, not batch-applied on the strength of the relation alone -- the relation is a candidate SIGNAL, not a verdict. 54 of 296 (18%) were coincidental strong_related links (e.g. "spear" surfaced via "camp", "honeycomb" via "Forest of Ephraim", the entire "word:*" sense-family via "wilderness") or data artifacts (8 items with a literal gloss of "None") or genuine unresolved ambiguity (Rephaim, Ephraim/G2187, Magog, Shelah, the four "King's" fragments) -- all excluded, not forced in.
